definition: Executive Dashboards is a core concept in Data Analytics. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Executive Dashboards is
theory.body: Executive Dashboards describes the methods and patterns used within Data Analytics to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Executive Dashboards is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Executive Dashboards matters
theory.body: Without Executive Dashboards, systems built with Data Analytics are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Executive Dashboards works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Executive Dashboards follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Executive Dashboards.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Executive Dashboards
theory.body: Executive Dashboards offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
